question.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le 2\}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]_{1}^{e}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
